messages:
maria: FYI alert from the audit ingest pipeline — write queue spiked around 22:06 UTC and we started dropping non-critical events. Investigating cause, but cost implications are getting ugly.
kevin: ugh. is this backpressure from ES ingest nodes or from the producer side (app buffers)?
maria: looks like a mix. producers are pushing bursts after a deploy, and our ES bulk indexing latencies jumped. ingest-bot: Indexer lag metric: audit_bulk_latency_p50=120ms p95=1.2s p99=4.8s. queue_depth=18k.
oliver: can we throttle at the producer to smooth bursts? what's our current producer batch config?
anita: producers use kafka-producer default batching; we set linger.ms=50 and batch.size ~ 100KB. topic partitions=24. spikes compress poorly because payloads are JSON with repetitive fields.
kevin: two quick levers: 1) increase batching/linger to build larger bulks, 2) switch audit events to newline-delimited protobuf or compressed msgpack to reduce network and ES parsing. both have tradeoffs for realtime.
maria: customers expect near-realtime audit events for compliance; can't just add 5-10s delays across the board. we need a hybrid policy: real-time for high-sev actions (RBAC changes, KMS key ops, login failures) and batched sampling for verbose events.
oliver: Agreed. Suggest: tag events with priority header. high-priority -> route to fast path index with smaller shards and higher refresh_rate. low-priority -> route to cold-topic with 30s batching and eventual indexing.
kevin: Implementation notes: ES bulk API sweet spot ~5-15MB per bulk request. aim for ~10MB compressed. Also avoid indexing full request/response bodies — store raw payloads in S3 and index metadata/refs. Big win for cost.
manual snippet from ops notes: `audit-producer.conf`: `linger.ms=200`, `batch.size=1048576`, `compression.type=gzip`, `max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=1`
anita: gzip helps but CPU on producers rises; offload compression to sidecar or use LZ4 for better CPU/size tradeoff.
security-oncall: What about schema changes? customers asked for additional fields in audit events (resource.owner, client_ip). Adding them to mapping increases index size and mapping churn. Any thoughts on dynamic fields?
maria: prefer explicit mapping. dynamic mapping will explode field cardinality. For client_ip we can store as ip field; for resource.owner add as keyword with limited cardinality and set doc_values=false if we won't aggregate.
kevin: also consider keeping a flattened 'annotations' kv blob (stored but not indexed) for arbitrary customer metadata — searchable only via reindex/ETL. avoids mapping pain.
oliver: validation: we should expose an API that validates customer-visible audit event schema before sending to us. lightweight validation service that enforces required fields and flags unsupported keys.
manual: `POST /v1/audit/validate` - returns permitted_index (high|low), size_estimate, recommended_compression. use as preflight in SDKs.
anita: cost side: ES storage is our biggest recurring cost. If we reduce indexed fields and move raw payloads to S3 with lifecycle to glacier after 90d, we save ~50% on storage bills. but adds retrieval latency for forensic requests.
maria: for compliance customers we can offer 'full indexing' as an enterprise add-on with higher retention and SLA. default self-serve accounts get metadata-only indexing.
security-oncall: Regarding backpressure handling: add explicit consumer lag monitors and circuit-breaker on producers. If indexer p95 > 2s, producers should enter controlled-shed mode where they sample non-essential events at 10%.
ops: quick math: at 1M events/day, full index ~2TB/month. metadata-only index ~120GB/month. moving payloads to S3 -> primary ES cost drops dramatically.
kevin: Ops action items: 1) create priority tagging spec for audit events (maria), 2) implement preflight validation endpoint + SDK integration (oliver), 3) experiment with producer compression/linger settings on staging with traffic replay (anita), 4) update ES indexing pipeline to route low-priority to cold index and store payloads in S3 (eng-infra).
maria: I'll draft the tagging spec and customer communication for any changes that affect delivery. Expect a short maintenance window for deploys to change producer defaults.
oliver: I'll prototype the validation API this week, will add opt-in flags in SDK so customers can validate before sending.
anita: will run load test Friday with `kafka-producer` harness: 100k eps for 10m, compare bulk sizes 1MB vs 8MB, gzip vs lz4. will post results.
security-oncall: Good. also prepare runbook for incident response if backpressure spikes again: alert thresholds, rollback knobs, feature flags to toggle rich-audit, and customer notification templates.
maria: tagging spec draft link: https://redwood.internal/docs/audit-tagging-draft (internal) 
kevin: one more thought — KMS ops: KMS key creation/deletion events must always be high-priority; they are compliance-sensitive. ensure they bypass sampling and get immutable storage with separate retention policy.
manual: ingest-bot: note added - KMS events route=priority-high, retention=3650d.
anita: thanks all. will update thread with load test numbers and cost delta table. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks — this looks actionable.
oliver: ping me when the validation API is ready for review.
security-oncall: closing loop once runbook and alerts are updated.
